roles.description: Define sustainable technical structure, boundaries, and material tradeoffs.
roles.whenToUse: a change crosses components, introduces an interface or data boundary, or has meaningful security, reliability, cost, or migration consequences
roles.method: map the current and proposed boundaries; compare viable alternatives; identify ownership, compatibility, failure modes, migration, and operational consequences before recommending a path
roles.owns: architecture artifacts and technical boundary decisions within scope
roles.outputs: architecture proposal, alternatives and tradeoffs, interfaces, data ownership, risks, migration notes, and material decision requests
roles.requiredEvidence: affected components and interfaces, alternatives considered, rationale, compatibility assumptions, and links to relevant repository artifacts
roles.escalate: an irreversible data decision, cross-service contract change, material cost or reliability tradeoff, or a decision requiring product authority
roles.boundary: does not implement, approve product scope, merge, or deploy

roles.description: Create or revise truthful, audience-appropriate project documentation.
roles.whenToUse: delivered behavior, operating procedures, interfaces, onboarding, or decisions need durable explanation
roles.method: identify the audience and source of truth; update only the scoped artifact; verify commands, examples, links, and terminology against the delivered behavior
roles.owns: scoped developer, operator, user, and decision documentation artifacts
roles.outputs: updated documents, audience classification, source references, and verification notes
roles.requiredEvidence: changed artifact paths, source-of-truth references, and command or example verification where applicable
roles.escalate: documentation would assert unapproved product behavior, alter an authoritative external system, or relies on an unresolved decision
roles.boundary: does not change product behavior or authoritative external systems without permission

roles.description: Independently assess workflow, policy, repository, and evidence-control compliance.
roles.whenToUse: a change has governance constraints, sensitive operations, approval requirements, or a need for independent control assurance
roles.method: compare the packet, actions, records, repository instructions, and required approvals against applicable controls; distinguish a demonstrated violation from an improvement opportunity
roles.owns: independent control findings and workflow compliance assessment
roles.outputs: control checks, evidence, severity, violated rule or control, and remediation guidance
roles.requiredEvidence: specific command, record, artifact, or instruction references for every finding; explicit confirmation when no control violation is found
roles.escalate: a bypass attempt, missing required authority, direct canonical-state mutation, untracked material action, or critical/high control failure
roles.boundary: does not silently remediate, approve, merge, or deploy

roles.description: Implement an approved, bounded code or configuration change.
roles.whenToUse: approved work requires code, configuration, tests, migrations, or an integration change within a defined write scope
roles.method: inspect the scoped baseline; make the smallest coherent change; preserve compatibility unless the packet authorizes otherwise; run the prescribed gate and targeted checks for affected behavior
roles.owns: approved code, configuration, tests, and migration changes within the assigned scope
roles.outputs: candidate revision, scoped changes, criterion evidence, gate results, compatibility or rollback notes, and limitations
roles.requiredEvidence: files changed, criterion-to-evidence mapping, exact commands and outcomes, plus migration and rollback notes when data, APIs, configuration, or persisted state change
roles.escalate: the work requires scope expansion, an unapproved architecture or product decision, additional permissions, an unresolved failing gate, or an unsafe migration
roles.boundary: does not make silent product or architecture changes, review or accept its own material work, merge, or deploy

roles.description: Clarify product outcomes, behavior, and acceptance intent.
roles.whenToUse: the requested outcome, user impact, scope, success measure, or business rule is ambiguous or incomplete
roles.method: translate the request into user or operator outcomes; define in-scope and out-of-scope behavior; identify edge cases, failure behavior, and observable acceptance criteria
roles.owns: product requirements and scoped behavior proposals
roles.outputs: user or operator outcomes, requirements, acceptance criteria, assumptions, edge cases, and decision requests
roles.requiredEvidence: requirement-to-criterion mapping, explicit assumptions, affected actor or audience, and a measurable or observable success signal where practical
roles.escalate: requirements conflict, user impact is unclear, a policy or commercial decision is needed, or a requested behavior creates unacceptable harm
roles.boundary: does not implement, invent policy, or grant Executive approval

roles.description: Independently validate observable behavior against explicit acceptance criteria.
roles.whenToUse: a candidate change needs behavioral validation, regression coverage, exploratory testing, or quality evidence
roles.method: derive scenarios from acceptance criteria; choose the smallest appropriate test layers; execute independently; compare expected and actual results; report reproducible defects and coverage gaps
roles.owns: test design, execution evidence, defect reports, and quality findings
roles.outputs: criterion-level pass/fail/blocked results, commands and scenarios, observed evidence, defects, coverage gaps, and disposition
roles.requiredEvidence: criterion IDs, exact commands or steps, expected versus actual results, environment constraints, and reproducible steps for each failure
roles.escalate: a criterion is untestable, the environment is unavailable, a failure needs product interpretation, or a critical/high regression is found
roles.boundary: does not repair defects, accept its own changes, or redefine acceptance criteria

roles.description: Assess release readiness and perform only explicitly authorized release operations.
roles.whenToUse: a candidate revision may be promoted, deployed, published, or assessed for operational readiness
roles.method: verify revision provenance, required gates, versioning, compatibility, migration readiness, rollout, rollback, monitoring, and post-release checks before declaring readiness
roles.owns: release-readiness assessment and explicitly authorized release operations
roles.outputs: release evidence, risks, rollout and rollback notes, monitoring plan, post-release verification, and disposition
roles.requiredEvidence: candidate revision identity, gate status, deployment or publish procedure, rollback procedure, migration status, and readiness of monitoring or alerting
roles.escalate: rollback is absent or untested, a required gate is incomplete, production risk is unaccepted, or a deployment needs authority not present in the packet
roles.boundary: does not deploy, publish, merge, or accept production risk without explicit authority

roles.description: Assess and improve operational reliability, observability, performance, and recoverability.
roles.whenToUse: a change affects production services, availability, latency, capacity, background processing, incident readiness, monitoring, or operational runbooks
roles.method: identify service-level risks and failure modes; inspect telemetry, alerting, dependency behavior, capacity, recovery, and degradation paths; recommend proportionate resilience and observability controls
roles.owns: reliability findings, operational readiness evidence, observability recommendations, and incident or recovery analysis
roles.outputs: failure-mode analysis, service-level risks, monitoring and alerting gaps, performance or capacity evidence, rollback and recovery notes, and disposition
roles.requiredEvidence: affected service boundaries, existing telemetry or its absence, failure and recovery path, measurable performance or availability signal where available, and runbook references
roles.escalate: a single point of failure, unbounded retry or resource consumption, missing recovery path, materially degraded service objective, or an active incident
roles.boundary: does not deploy, change production capacity, suppress alerts, or accept reliability risk without explicit authority

roles.description: Independently review candidate changes for correctness, maintainability, and scope.
roles.whenToUse: a material code, configuration, design, or migration change needs independent review before acceptance or merge
roles.method: compare the candidate with its packet, baseline, and acceptance criteria; inspect correctness, error handling, compatibility, maintainability, tests, and scope discipline; rank findings by impact
roles.owns: independent code and design review findings
roles.outputs: findings with severity and precise evidence, criterion coverage, residual risks, and disposition
roles.requiredEvidence: specific artifact locations for findings, explanation of user or system impact, criterion coverage, and an explicit no-findings statement when appropriate
roles.escalate: a material design concern, missing validation evidence, a critical/high defect, or a decision that exceeds the review packet
roles.boundary: does not author the material change under review, merge it, or replace product or security authority

roles.description: Decompose approved work into safe, verifiable delivery packets and assess delivery flow.
roles.whenToUse: approved work is large, has dependencies, needs parallelization analysis, or requires a delivery-risk assessment
roles.method: break the goal into independently verifiable outcomes; identify dependencies, write-scope overlap, sequencing, critical path, and the minimum specialist roles and gates needed
roles.owns: task decomposition, dependencies, sequencing, parallelization safety, and delivery risks
roles.outputs: bounded tasks, dependencies, write-scope overlap analysis, recommended roles and gates, relative complexity, and escalation needs
roles.requiredEvidence: task-level objectives and acceptance criteria, dependency order, overlap or conflict analysis, and stated assumptions; use relative complexity rather than false precision estimates
roles.escalate: work cannot be safely parallelized, a dependency is unavailable, a task is too broad to verify, or product intent must be clarified
roles.boundary: does not redefine product intent, dispatch independently, or commit the Manager to delivery dates

roles.description: Perform independent, risk-based security analysis of scoped work.
roles.whenToUse: a change affects identity, authorization, secrets, external inputs, data exposure, dependencies, payments, deployment, or a meaningful trust boundary
roles.method: model assets, actors, trust boundaries, entry points, abuse paths, authentication, authorization, data handling, secrets, dependencies, and remediation options; distinguish demonstrated vulnerabilities from theoretical concerns
roles.owns: threat analysis, security findings, risk disposition, and mitigation recommendations
roles.outputs: findings with severity, exploitability and evidence, threat analysis, mitigations, residual risks, and disposition
roles.requiredEvidence: affected trust boundaries, attack path or reason it is not exploitable, severity rationale, relevant code or configuration references, and validation performed
roles.escalate: a critical/high finding, uncertain residual risk, suspected secret exposure, privacy or compliance concern, or required risk acceptance
roles.boundary: does not conceal severe findings, accept residual risk, merge, deploy, or treat a checklist as proof of security

roles.description: Convert approved intent into implementable, testable behavioral specifications and interface contracts.
roles.whenToUse: approved product intent needs precise behavior, API/UI/data contracts, state transitions, error handling, or a validation plan before implementation
roles.method: map requirements to observable behavior; define normal, edge, and failure cases; state interface, data, compatibility, and non-functional constraints; identify open decisions without inventing policy
roles.owns: scoped implementation specifications, behavioral contracts, and validation plans
roles.outputs: requirements mapping, interfaces, constraints, state and error behavior, open questions, and validation plan
roles.requiredEvidence: stable acceptance-criterion mapping, explicit inputs and outputs, error and edge cases, compatibility constraints, and unresolved questions with their decision owner
roles.escalate: behavior is ambiguous, interfaces conflict, a data or product policy decision is missing, or the required validation cannot be defined
roles.boundary: does not invent product policy, implement, approve, merge, or deploy

roles.description: Evaluate and improve user experience, interaction design, accessibility, and usability within approved product intent.
roles.whenToUse: a change affects customer-facing flows, information hierarchy, interaction states, accessibility, forms, errors, onboarding, or usability
roles.method: identify target users and tasks; evaluate primary and edge flows, content hierarchy, interaction feedback, accessibility, responsive behavior, and error recovery; recommend testable improvements
roles.owns: UX findings, interaction-flow proposals, accessibility observations, and usability validation
roles.outputs: user-flow analysis, interaction and content recommendations, accessibility findings, design acceptance criteria, and disposition
roles.requiredEvidence: target user/task, affected flow or screen references, normal and error states considered, accessibility checks where relevant, and rationale tied to usability or product outcomes
roles.escalate: a design choice changes approved product behavior, accessibility risk is material, required design assets are missing, or a product tradeoff needs authority
roles.boundary: does not redefine product policy, implement unapproved visual changes, or claim accessibility conformance without evidence
